# Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity (PSH)

PSH is a disorder in the regulation of autonomic function with acute brain injury, most notably severe TBI.

-   Recurrent episodes of excessive sympathetic activity that start rapidly, are often induced by stimulation, and resolve spontaneously after a variable period of time or after administration of an abortive medication
-   Core clinical features include tachycardia, hypertension, tachypnea, hyperthermia, sweating, and/or increased muscle tone with possible dystonic posturing
-   Associated conditions --- brain trauma, nontraumatic forms of acute brain disease, including anoxic-ischemic coma after cardiac arrest, intracranial hemorrhage, autoimmune encephalitis, ischemic stroke, hydrocephalus, and cerebral fat embolism syndrome

## PSH Assessment Measure

### Clinical Feature Scale (CFS)

| Clinical Feature                  | 0          | 1                                                 | 2                                             | 3                                                    | Score |
|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Heart rate (BPM)                  | \<100      | 100 to 119                                        | 120 to 139                                    | ≥140                                                 |       |
| Respiratory rate (breaths/minute) | \<18       | 18 to 23                                          | 24 to 29                                      | ≥30                                                  |       |
| Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)    | \<140      | 140 to 159                                        | 160 to 179                                    | ≥180                                                 |       |
| Temperature (°C)                  | \<37       | 37 to 37.8                                        | 38 to 38.9                                    | ≥39                                                  |       |
| Sweating                          | nil (none) | mild (moist skin)                                 | moderate (beads of sweat)                     | severe (profuse generalized sweating)                |       |
| Posturing during episodes         | nil (none) | mild (increased tone but not requiring treatment) | moderate (increased tone requiring treatment) | severe (very increased tone refractory to treatment) |       |

**CFS subtotal =**

### Diagnosis Likelihood Tool (DLT)

**Score as "1" if present**

-   Clinical features occur simultaneously
-   Episodes are paroxysmal in nature
-   Their reactivity to normally nociceptive stimuli
-   Features persist ≥3 consecutive days
-   Features persist ≥2 weeks post-brain injury
-   Features persist despite treatment of differential diagnoses
-   Medications administered to decrease sympathetic features
-   ≥3 episodes daily
-   Absence of parasympathetic features during episodes
-   Absence of other presumed cause of features
-   Antecedent acquired brain injury

**Combined total (CFS + DLT) =**

**Interpretation**\
- 0-6 = not unlikely\
- 8-16 = possible\
- ≥17 = PSH probable

**Total score 8 or greater, then use the CFS scale for monitoring of evolution (document daily maximal score).**

### Abortive Medications

#### IV Route

| Drug             | Mechanism                       | Dose                                                                                   | Clinical effect                                                        | Side effects                                                                          |
|-------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|
| Morphine sulfate | Opioid agonist\*                | 2 to 8 mg IV bolus                                                                     | Abortive -- Improves most features                                     | Respiratory depression, Sedation, Hypotension, Pruritus, Histamine release, Tolerance |
| Propofol         | GABA-A agonist                  | 15 to 20 mg IV bolus or continuous infusion (up to 80 mcg/kg/min)                      | Abortive (bolus) -- Improves most features                             | Deep sedation (intubated patients only), Propofol infusion syndrome                   |
| Benzodiazepines  | GABA-A agonists                 | Diazepam 5--10 mg IV bolus<br>Lorazepam 1--4 mg IV bolus<br>Midazolam 2--5 mg IV bolus | Abortive -- Can improve most features (less effectively than morphine) | Sedation, Respiratory depression, Tolerance                                           |
| Dantrolene       | Ryanodine receptors in myocytes | 0.5 to 2 mg/kg IV every 6--12 hours (up to 10 mg/kg total daily)                       | Improves hypertonicity and dystonia                                    | Hepatotoxicity (can be severe), Respiratory depression, Muscle weakness               |

#### Enteral / PO Route

| Drug            | Mechanism       | Dose                                 | Clinical effect       | Side effects                                |
|-------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|
| Benzodiazepines | GABA-A agonists | Clonazepam 0.5 to 2 mg every 8 hours | Abortive / preventive | Sedation, Respiratory depression, Tolerance |

### Preventive Medications

#### IV Route

| Drug            | Mechanism                          | Dose                                      | Clinical effect                          | Side effects                              |
|--------------|--------------|------------------|--------------|--------------|
| Propofol        | GABA-A agonist                     | Continuous infusion (up to 80 mcg/kg/min) | Preventive -- Improves most features     | Deep sedation, Propofol infusion syndrome |
| Dexmedetomidine | Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist | 0.2 to 1.5 mcg/kg/hour by IV infusion     | Improves mostly tachycardia/hypertension | Bradycardia, Hypotension, Sedation        |

#### Enteral / PO Route

| Drug          | Mechanism                             | Dose                                                        | Clinical effect                                           | Side effects                                                      |
|--------------|---------------|----------------|--------------|--------------|
| Clonidine     | Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist    | 0.1 to 0.3 mg every 6--8 hours                              | Abortive and preventive                                   | Bradycardia, Hypotension, Sedation                                |
| Propranolol†  | Noncardioselective beta blocker       | 20 to 80 mg every 4--6 hours                                | Improves tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, dystonia | Bradycardia, Sleep disturbances                                   |
| Gabapentin    | Alpha-2-delta calcium channel subunit | 100--300 mg every 8 hours (titrate up to 3600--4800 mg/day) | Improves most features                                    | Mild sedation                                                     |
| Bromocriptine | Dopamine D2 receptor agonist          | 1.25 mg every 12 hours (titrate up to 40 mg/day)            | Modest and delayed effect                                 | Agitation, Confusion, Dyskinesia, Nausea, Orthostatic hypotension |
| Baclofen      | GABA-B agonist                        | 5 mg every 8 hours (titrate up to 80 mg/day)                | Improves hypertonicity and dystonia                       | Sedation, Muscle weakness, Withdrawal risk                        |
